wording.engine_summary: Runs an installed Windows 11 Arm desktop on BridgeVM's own Hypervisor.framework VMM with persistent storage, display/input, dynamic resolution, network, audio, clipboard and folder integration, TPM/Secure Boot workflows, snapshots, window Coherence verbs and experimental 3D. Every release-blocking criterion is proven by live evidence; known open defects are disclosed below.
wording.machine_contract: QEMU virt-compatible guest contract with documented deviations

criteria.title: Cold boot reliability
criteria.statement: At least 9 of 10 cold boots report stage4_pass=1 AND firstboot_fresh=1 in firstboot-stage.txt.
criteria.measured: PROVEN 2026-08-10 at 0f02579: the product-default Apple in-kernel-GIC fresh-firstboot P1 gate passed 10/10, above the fixed 9/10 threshold. Every independent APFS clone recorded stage4_pass=1, firstboot_fresh=1, last_stage=stage4, three SYSTEM_RESET transitions, clean SYSTEM_OFF and zero stalls; all ten firstboot hashes were distinct. Historical record: eight instrumented 5-boot soaks (14/40 aggregate) with owning-thread GIC reads at every terminal stall. Two failure shapes fully characterized: UEFI (PPI pending at GICR, CPU interface open/idle, never taken) and kernel (CNTV_CTL ISTATUS=0 with CVAL millions of ticks past -- the fire never forms). Historical correction 2026-08-11: RPR=0x10/AP1R0 with banked GICR_ISACTIVER0=0 did not prove an empty active set because shared SPI/MSI active state lives in distributor GICD_ISACTIVER*. Clearing the APR changed readback to rpr=0xff but was not a proven-safe correction and did not resume delivery; exact run 20260811-140847 later reached a Hypervisor.framework EOI-order trap after such a clear, so the mutation was removed. Every host lever tried and measured: unmask, CVAL rewrites, mask pulse, forced ISPENDR0 (delivers -- boot dies anyway; falsified as cure), ICC APR clear. ICH list registers unreadable (EL2 view unavailable). Defect isolated to Apple's in-kernel GICv3/vtimer under hv_vcpus_exit pressure; no public API re-arms forwarding. Apple Feedback draft ready (a1-apple-feedback-draft-20260806.md); remaining host option: relocate guest wake onto an owned device interrupt. 2026-08-07: EL2 avenue measured (strictly worse -- parks before first serial byte with zero exits/window) and wake-relocation closed by inference (waking the CPU is not the gap: 69k re-entries did not help, and even delivered timer interrupts did not save the boot). Every host-side avenue is now measured or closed by measurement-backed inference; the remaining path is Apple (Feedback draft ready, owner files). 2026-08-08 CONTROL EXPERIMENT: QEMU 11.0.2 accel=hvf on the SAME host boots the SAME canonical image 10/10 to the image's own bvagent READY (18-24s/boot, clean agent-driven poweroffs) -- QEMU links zero hv_gic_* symbols and emulates the GICv3 in userspace, driving hv_vcpu_set_pending_interrupt per run. Host kernel, vtimer surface and guest image exonerated; the defect is specific to the in-kernel GICv3. A host-side exit that does not wait on Apple now exists: swap the full-VM path to the codebase's userspace GICv3 (probe_mmio gic_* + platform/apple/firmware_irq.rs pattern). Evidence: a1-qemu-userspace-gic-control-20260808.md. 2026-08-08 USERSPACE-GIC SWAP LANDED: full userspace GICv3 (userspace_gic/ + usgic_bridge) behind BRIDGEVM_USERSPACE_GIC=1; zero hv_gic_* calls. Seven guest-contract findings fixed (PFR0.GIC advertise, WAKER storage-only, Group1 reset, PMCCNTR fastfail, edge-latched vtimer PPI w/ EOI-driven unmask, CNTPCT passthrough, SMP routing). Soak: 10/10 installed boots to BVAGENT READY (82-87s) with agent-driven PSCI SYSTEM_OFF, vs 14/40 on the in-kernel GIC. The A1 mechanism is absent by construction. Remaining for the criterion: the fresh-firstboot p1 gate (9/10 stage4_pass+fresh) on this configuration. Evidence: a1-userspace-gic-swap-20260808.md. Same-day scope note: usgic carried A15 to PROVEN (100/100), but venus 3D on usgic is not healthy -- first a real viogpu3d bug (D1 EXECUTE on pageable PAGE-section code at DISPATCH_LEVEL; DPE=1 stops it), then a vkCreateInstance wedge (CTX_CREATE + attach loop, zero SUBMIT_3D; hv_gic runs SUBMIT_3D immediately and A2 re-passes 58.82). MSI-X delivery verified in the ring; divergence is later in the venus fence/event chain. hv_gic stays default until resolved. That historical open note is superseded for A1 by the 2026-08-10 product-default in-kernel-GIC 10/10 fresh-firstboot gate.

criteria.title: Vulkan title frame rate
criteria.statement: A real Vulkan title reports guest-side samples>0 AND p50>=30 FPS.
criteria.measured: PROVEN 2026-08-08: verify-vulkan-title-fps.sh PASS x3 (samples/p50: 2511/58.82, 2528/58.82, 2531/58.82; source=setframebuf-intervals) on canonical-a2-staged-20260807 with venus_icd_loaded from the DriverStore, real content (cube.iso), foreground window, 45s windows. Final instrument defect: this PPSSPP binary never emits 'fps:' lines at any loglevel (measured 3/5/6, 7.9MB D-level log) -- the gate now derives per-frame samples from the title's own sceDisplaySetFrameBuf DEBUG lines (each flip interval = one frame time). The Vulkan path was never slow (~59 FPS p50 through venus); what looked like a 'Vulkan-startup wedge' was A1-class session mortality AROUND a working gate (1 of 4 final-day sessions still parked). History: 2026-08-06 instrument chain repair (bd31835..2ab575d); 2026-08-07 11 attempts 0 samples all A1-parked; retraction of an invalid falsification (6b8df9d) after finding the wrapper scrubbed BRIDGEVM_AGENT_WAKE_MS.

criteria.measured: PROVEN 2026-08-12 by live campaign 20260812-173200-91503-26516 on exact head 31368a1fc55abc8f3421d5b11b2e537c4f96a6f2: run_count=3, passes=3, failures=0, threshold_fps=30.0, fps_samples=[2633, 5275, 5369], fps_p50=[250.0, 62.5, 62.5], receipt SHA-256 8430c7d682c81330da3c2d969eb57ddd1c381c2dc59edc2fe094657a9f93a21e. No threshold, sampler, renderer, timeout or the 3/3 policy was relaxed.

criteria.title: No regression
criteria.statement: Workspace, Venus lib, probe example and Swift suites plus fmt, clippy, budgets and docs gates all pass at the final release head.
criteria.measured: PROVEN 2026-08-24 at tested head 48266df2aa32869429a3d3b6c81afe6551f27aa4 (branch agent/b4-descriptor-chain-evidence). Exact-SHA Studio T0 job 20260824-020223-18301-20930 ran all 28 check-project sections on Mac16,9 / macOS 26.5.2: every code, test, formatting, structural, documentation, installer and release-override step passed; the sole failure was the intentionally stale A11 registry that this docs-only update refreshes. scripts/run-xctest-shim-suites.sh reported 419 + 198 (1 skip) + 62 = 679 passed, 0 failed. The complete check log has SHA-256 b5142af0de23252312fc31d732e03466ebfa16dde7958c99a668f0abcbcbe1a1. The tested head adds sampled, structure-only virtio-gpu descriptor-chain rejection evidence so the next stable-black B4 lane can separate a guest that never posted RESOURCE_ATTACH_BACKING from BridgeVM consuming a malformed chain; existing used-length-zero consumption is unchanged. Security review bounded the event at the existing first-64/each-1024 sampling policy and converted descriptor-table GPA overflow from a possible release panic into a typed rejection. It logs no guest address or payload. The first queued T0 attempt 20260824-014232-7277-25754 was correctly refused by the immutable worker guard (result=refused-free-space, available_gib=99); the guard was not relaxed, and space came only from two uncited failed 2026-08-06 job directories. B4 remains OPEN: t8 job 20260824-003132-73288-13833 at main 697477f failed landed 15/20 with p95 709 ms. Four staleness conditions are checked rather than remembered: the registry fails when crates/, runners/, apps/, scripts/ or tests/ differ between tested_commit and HEAD, when a measured entry cites a head other than tested_commit, when tested_commit names no known commit in a full clone, and when a claimed test or step count differs from the tests and steps that actually exist. Resealed 2026-08-24 at 6613feb0d50b09f9517643942e929e09b4734471 after the unbacked-TRANSFER3D renderer containment: exact-SHA T0 job 20260824-102807-48651-3943 ran all 28 sections with only the intentional stale-A11 registry failure, shim suites 679/679, check log SHA-256 08574af98bafae5598c2dcf865c4e56c5830c08f45dc8ec44adac2bc2b5f67ce. The immediately preceding T0 at the same code head (20260824-101248-42222-8036, check log SHA-256 093a183780a943cfa07e4b091f79b0cea5e263e7ee661f48dc55633446d151a6) is recorded rather than hidden: it additionally failed ControlModelLifecycleTests.testStopDuringStartupWaitsForProcessThenStopsIt, a wall-clock race in a Swift UI lifecycle test whose fake backend flips isRunning() via asyncAfter(startVisibilityDelay: 0.2) on a global queue; it was reproduced as a load flake by 3/3 clean reruns of the full shim suites (679/679 each) at the identical commit and has no code path to the Rust virtio-gpu change. Resealed 2026-08-24 at 8acb81b132d584d791ad4a3ab40a4432c9d59099 after tightening two structural ceilings to their real measured size (scripts/ is a freshness CODE_PATH, so a budgets-only edit still requires re-proof): exact-SHA T0 job 20260824-142248-36798-330 ran all 28 sections with only the intentional stale-A11 registry failure, shim suites 679/679, check log SHA-256 df8f7c5f18d9e70af511b06fabbdef7103c6f5962d12d0e15d3420c373a75da0. criteria.title: Secure SMCCC TRNG
criteria.statement: Guest TRNG_RND_32/64 are served only by the host OS CSPRNG; no exit-count, time, PID or constant-derived fallback exists, and provider failure returns NO_ENTROPY.
criteria.measured: The protocol lives in bridgevm_hvf::smccc_trng over SecRandomCopyBytes, with one dispatch shared by the primary and secondary loops. 14 tests cover the DEN 0098 register layout, bit masking, request limits, FEATURES discovery and the fail-closed paths; the exit-counter generator and the duplicated probe constants are deleted. Guest-visible behaviour is not yet re-measured on a live boot.

criteria.title: PSCI 1.1 conformance
criteria.statement: CPU_ON and AFFINITY_INFO implement the specified state table, affinity levels and error codes with atomic state transitions.
criteria.measured: State logic lives in bridgevm_hvf::psci with 13 tests covering the CPU_ON table, affinity levels 0-3, cluster aggregation, CPU0, RES1 spellings and invalid targets/levels. CPU_ON reports ON_PENDING for a pending CPU, AFFINITY_INFO reads X2 and searches the whole topology, and the state check and Off->OnPending transition share one critical section. Live 1/2/4-vCPU topology validation is not yet run.

criteria.title: Typed product runtime
criteria.statement: The product app and hvf-runner drive a typed runtime API from a versioned launch manifest instead of executing an example binary through shell.
criteria.measured: PROVEN 2026-08-07 with a GUI-driven session: the packaged BridgeVMControl.app launched a library VM through hvf-runner --launch-spec (log: 'launching through the typed runtime'), the guest booted to BVAGENT READY on the app's shipping device shape (virgl 0x1050, TPM2 TIS on the runtime-owned swtpm with the Keychain-derived key, agent console, evidence surfaces incl. launch-manifest.json), and an agent-console shutdown ended in PSCI SYSTEM_OFF with a clean process exit. Foundation: 24 R1 slices (f545fd0..fbb2fa3) -- typed manifest validation, pre-launch writer leases, env_clear allowlist spawn, run_vm generations with flush+receipt, DeviceSurfaces env parity, supervisor-owned swtpm (key over fd 0, wrong key refused), watchdog-less app mode, runnerArguments() vector pinned by the 188-test suite. Fixed on the way: ad-hoc builds cannot use the data-protection keychain (errSecMissingEntitlement on WRITES only -- the probe must be a real add), so the key store falls back to the login keychain for unentitled builds. Wrapper script remains as the source-checkout fallback only.

criteria.title: Process-recreate reset
criteria.statement: 100 consecutive guest SYSTEM_RESETs each produce a new helper PID, an increasing reset generation, a fresh guest boot marker and 4 online CPUs.
criteria.measured: 2026-08-08 PROVEN on the userspace GICv3 (BRIDGEVM_USERSPACE_GIC=1): CYCLES=100 verify-reset-recreate.sh PASS -- 100 consecutive guest SYSTEM_RESETs, each producing a fresh helper PID (predecessor gone), increasing generation 1..100, fresh agent READY and online_cpus=4; reset.receipt generation 100 with disk+vars flushed. Zero A1 parks in 100 consecutive full boots (~4.7h). Prior in-kernel-GIC best: 8 cycles/13 generations before a UEFI park. Run: reset-recreate-usgic3-151732. Evidence: a15-reset-recreate-100-20260808.md.

criteria.title: Release security and storage hardening
criteria.statement: Release builds launch only bundled signed helpers, verify socket peer UID, hold an exclusive disk/vars lease and use positional atomic disk I/O.
criteria.measured: Overrides: scripts/check-release-overrides.sh inspects compiled objects and reports 4 overrides debug-only, PASS. Bundled signed helper: HelperCodeSignature.swift requires the swtpm helper to share the app team ID, with 10 swift-testing tests. Peer UID: crates/bridgevm-daemon/src/peer_credentials.rs with tests. Exclusive lease: crates/bridgevm-hvf/src/media_lock.rs. Positional atomic disk I/O: every seek+read on a data path is now read_exact_at/write_all_at -- nvme/disk.rs (read, write-back write, and the copy-on-write chunk fault), probe_mmio/virtio_backend.rs, virtio_blk/media_backend.rs and windows_arm/uefi_io.rs, whose write_all_at/read_exact_at were named for positional I/O while seeking. Three tests park the shared file offset at 4096, perform a read, a write-back write and an overlay fault, and require it to still be 4096; falsified by restoring seek+read, which reports the offset moved to 1536. The one remaining seek is in media_lock.rs, rewriting the lock file's holder line, which is not a data path.

criteria.title: Nonblocking provenance-sealed live queue
criteria.statement: Long gates run asynchronously on the Studio local queue with sealed commit/image/vars hashes and no foreground wait beyond 120 seconds.
criteria.measured: The Studio local queue (com.ketchio.bridgevm-live LaunchAgent, StartInterval 60s, no inbound listener and no runner registration) has run 121 completed jobs across tiers t0-t5 plus t1-snapshot and t1-restore-boot, counted from ~/BridgeVM/live-queue/done. Submission returns a job id immediately and never waits. Receipts seal the commit and, for tiers that read one, the image and vars: job 20260805-115614-86173-14911 records disk_sha256 6fef8f980adbc6af1ed41a1934d1ebafd93b8a1b4d2ab9a3f8bd07ae950d9b54 and vars_sha256 d329b5b03cc5673435d3949f1b5b5b2bfe3f4dfe1f6f0b56ca5894f3bce87d3f against the real 64 GiB pair, re-read from the job directory 2026-08-16. The field is disk_sha256; this criterion previously called it image_sha256. Nine defects were found by running the queue rather than by reasoning about it.

criteria.title: Claim consistency
criteria.statement: README, STATUS, core descriptors, CLI and app wording are generated from or checked against this registry, and a deterministic check fails on drift.
criteria.measured: README and STATUS carry generated blocks rendered from this registry and never hand-edited; render-capability-status.py --check fails on any drift between them. The forbidden-claim scan covers whole trees (crates/**/*.rs excluding /target/, apps/macos/Sources/**/*.swift) plus README, STATUS, AGENTS.md, docs/hvf-windows-engine-strategy.md and the capability matrix prose, replacing a hand-kept six-file list that silently stopped covering anything added or moved. Falsified during the original widening: appending '// Windows beta' to crates/bridgevm-cli/src/main.rs made the check fail; it was not caught before the widening. 2026-08-20 correction: the post-release scan also retires stale 'the product is Engineering Preview' present-tense wording, which had survived in AGENTS.md after the 1.0 promotion. A mechanical promotion guard also refuses to raise product_state while any release-blocking criterion is unproven. Evidence: docs/windows-arm/capability-matrix.md.

criteria.title: Disk safety
criteria.statement: Powered-off snapshot export and restore keep a byte-exact atomic disk plus vars pair under an explicit byte quota.
criteria.measured: Restore-boot proven by live-queue job 20260805-091656-10876-16297 (tier t1-restore-boot, outcome completed, pass true, commit e8eb8b9e3ac7, Mac16,9 / macOS 26.5.2) against the real 64 GiB image: create.txt records disk_bytes 68719476736 and disk_sha256 56b1361282933f2cf3e409604cdc2da81f8c6ad8536de2bdcc472818e204280d. The guest-observed marker goes BV-NO-MARKER before the write, BV-ORIGINAL-1785935910 after the disk is clobbered, and the identical BV-ORIGINAL-1785935910 after restore, so the restore returns state a guest process can read rather than a file that merely hashes correctly. The remaining acceptance items are covered by tier t1-snapshot through scripts/verify-powered-off-snapshot.sh, a different job.

criteria.title: Pointer click reliability
criteria.statement: Across 20 independent APFS-clone boots of the installed guest, a host-injected absolute pointer click on the same real Windows UI target lands 20/20: press and release both consumed by the guest, zero duplicate clicks, zero stuck buttons, correct coordinates, and visible-response latency p95 <= 250 ms.
criteria.known_defect: Pointer clicks are unreliable: in the latest 10-boot live batch the host delivered every click but Windows acted on only 1 of 10. Keyboard input is unaffected. Tracked as criterion B4.
criteria.measured: Batched 2026-08-17: ten fresh boots, HID fired 10/10, guest reacted 1/10 (run 7 at first_changed_ms=1000); every failing run had the dialog on screen and a byte-identical 1000ms capture. Pacing raised 30->300ms scored 0/3, killing the plan's prime suspect. Per-interface protocol is correct (pointer=report, 6-byte absolute), and every host-visible counter -- doorbells, rings, interrupts -- is identical between a landed and a lost click, so the loss is strictly guest-side beyond host instrumentation. Open as a product defect; the 20/20 acceptance gate above was fixed 2026-08-20 before any fix attempt, and next steps need guest-side tooling (ETW/transfer-ring completion). Historical note: this criterion was previously titled 'Pointer latency measured' with a record-a-measurement statement, and was marked PROVEN on the strength of having recorded the 1/10 batch; that classification let user-facing wording read as working pointer input and was retracted -- the criterion is OPEN until the reliability gate passes. Batched 2026-08-20 against the fixed gate (t8 job 20260820-134138-21205-18560 at 13e83a58d0e423e8b4ad9cac4d53f62b1436c234, gate log SHA-256 b34c42ca…, honest FAIL, landed 0/20): the host emitted move+button+release for 20/20 with zero rejections and zero drain-block traces, while the in-guest GetAsyncKeyState probe spanning every click window saw zero button transitions in 20/20 — the input stack never received the report, falsifying foreground-routing and application-side loss and localising the defect between the posted transfer event and the HID class driver (details and two instrument caveats in docs/windows-arm/evidence/b4-pointer-reliability-batch-20260820.md). Batched 2026-08-23 against the same fixed gate (t8 job 20260823-054152-13053-2622 at main commit 31df3c313bfa925d215883394d407950e25ae1d2, gate log SHA-256 3c9f7d72…, summary SHA-256 4192f7b0…, honest FAIL, landed 17/20, p95_first_changed_ms=531 against the 250 ms limit). This is the first batch to run all 20 runs instead of being cancelled, and it moves the defect: the 17 landed runs each show fired=true press=1 release=1 stuck=0, exactly one click at the expected coordinates and a real active CGL IOSurface reaction, so a host click now reaches the Windows input stack. The landed first-change times are bimodal (169-248 ms for seven runs, 314-531 ms for ten), which is presentation cost after a press Windows has already consumed, not lost input. The three non-landing runs are three refusals rather than lost clicks: run 10 never wrote a target ready line (invalid-target), and runs 9 and 19 reached a valid ready line and BVPTR_READY at the button centre but the watcher refused with 'active target baseline not presented', so no click was injected at all (their input.ctl ends at POINTER move and dci5_emission count is zero). B4 stays OPEN on two separately measured problems: the guest target must present and hold deterministically, and the post-click presentation path costs roughly twice the budget in half the runs. Batched 2026-08-23 again (t8 job 20260823-113151-99719-9275 at main 8e1f38791008da6b3fa20c437ca0a42065a076c5, gate log SHA-256 b28ec56e…, summary SHA-256 93b30989…, honest FAIL, landed 13/20, p95 660 ms). This head carried a print-only observation of a DCI5 report still queued past its own deadline, and in all three runs where it fired the printed lateness matched the independently measured hold overshoot within 0.5 ms (94.8/95.0, 169.5/169.0, 43.4/43.6 ms): the report was eligible and waiting, so the drain ran late. The hold overshoot is therefore a missed host wake, not an unready guest TD. Ten further runs overshot without printing, which is the instrument's blind spot (it prints only from the automation pass that arms the next deadline). Target presentation also regressed: 6 runs refused with invalid-click-count and 1 with invalid-target while the probe reported a valid interactive desktop and its cursor at the button centre, so the white target never converged. Batched 2026-08-24 with target-baseline evidence (t8 job 20260824-003132-73288-13833 at main 697477f93b14b1b1317319784d6490ae19954924, gate log SHA-256 bdea989a…, summary SHA-256 191137cc…, honest FAIL, landed 15/20, p95 709 ms). Four refusals had valid 1600x900 target-ready records but a stable all-black active IOSurface for 120 seconds (peak_white_px=0); one separate run never wrote target-ready. The black path still completed IOSurface blits and paced CPU readbacks, whose retained 1600x900 checkpoints were also all black, so the renderer scanout source—not CGL publication or the blit—was black. All four stable-black lanes enter 203-322 persistent ctx-7 SUBMIT_3D failures beginning with VIRGL_CCMD_TRANSFER3D status 22 against an existing but unbacked resource; create and context attach exist, but no successful RESOURCE_ATTACH_BACKING precedes the first failure. The failure starts before the target/1600x900 transition. Fourteen of fifteen landed lanes have zero failed submits; landed run 10 has seven transient ctx-5 failures and recovers, so the earlier unqualified claim that successful runs had zero was retracted. PR #69 instruments the one remaining boundary: whether BridgeVM consumed a malformed descriptor chain at used length zero or the guest never posted the missing backing attach. Batched 2026-08-24 against the same fixed gate, the first batch to run with the unbacked-TRANSFER3D renderer containment merged (t8 job 20260824-115428-72165-14984 at main fcb95a59c5c63527564c0e54f479c3d05950ef0e, honest FAIL, landed 12/20, p95_first_changed_ms=688 against the 250 ms limit). Six lanes were stable black with result=baseline-not-presented and peak_white_px=0 (never painted); the ctx-7 renderer poison still separates black from landed perfectly and exclusively (181-240 failed ctx-7 submits per black lane, zero in all fourteen non-black lanes), while SET_SCANOUT errors were tested as a separator and rejected because they occur in all twenty lanes including every landed run. The containment demonstrably works where it applies -- in run 3 the never-backed constant buffer 153 was refused at seq 1641 and the next ctx-7 submit succeeded, so that context was not poisoned -- but it is not sufficient: the same lanes then fail on VIRGL_CCMD_DRAW_VBO with ENOTRECOVERABLE (run 3 seq 2198), and two black lanes (runs 1 and 7) never trip the preflight at all because their first failure is VIRGL_CCMD_COPY_TRANSFER3D. B4 is therefore NOT improved by this change and stays OPEN; the next measurement is COPY_TRANSFER3D and the DRAW_VBO ENOTRECOVERABLE path, not another pointer-timing change. Details in docs/windows-arm/evidence/b4-pointer-reliability-batch-20260820.md. Batched 2026-08-24 again with the containment widened from constant buffers to any PIPE_BUFFER (t8 job 20260824-154650-73552-15846 at main c3aa70244968377eb9d4116311bb86cde482ea30, gate log SHA-256 4c96a7ee…, summary SHA-256 8652c8a1…, honest FAIL, landed 11/20, p95 540 ms). The widening worked as written -- the preflight now fires in every stable-black lane where the narrower rule matched only half -- but the black-lane count stayed at 6/20, so B4 is not improved. The batch produced the decisive measurement instead: in four of six black lanes the first renderer failure is DRAW_VBO with status 104 (ENOTRECOVERABLE), which vrend_draw_vbo returns only from 'if (ctx->in_error)' before validating anything, and in run 4 there are zero ctx-7 submits between the preflight rejection (seq 3087, which never calls the renderer) and that draw (seq 3107). The context was therefore already erroneous, poisoned by a command inside an earlier submit that BridgeVM recorded as OK_NODATA, because virgl_submit_cmd succeeds for the buffer while vrend_report_context_error sets in_error from 85 call sites without failing it. The unbacked TRANSFER3D is an early visible symptom, not the originating fault, and the next step is to surface the first context error rather than the first failed submit. Details in docs/windows-arm/evidence/b4-pointer-reliability-batch-20260820.md.
